excerpt: Hot Pepper chili is a long chili variety. The Philippine Seed Board approved it in 1984. It takes 60 to 80 days from transplanting to the first harvest, with 7.79 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

Hot Pepper chili takes 60 to 80 days from transplanting to the first harvest. A shorter crop frees the field sooner and dodges more of the weather, while a longer one often fills more.

Trial yields come from well managed plots, so your own will depend on water, fertilizer, pests and timing.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?

blocks.text: It was weak against leafhopper, aphids, thrips, so scout for them from the early weeks. Read up on [eggplant leafhopper](/pests/eggplant-leafhopper), [bacterial wilt](/diseases/bacterial-wilt), [thrips](/pests/thrips).

The pests and diseases that hit chili fields most often: [tomato leaf curl](/diseases/tomato-leaf-curl), [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose), [Cercospora leaf spot](/diseases/cercospora-leaf-spot), [Corn earworm](/pests/corn-earworm), [cutworm](/pests/cutworm). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
Where and when to plant Hot Pepper chili

It is recommended for both the wet and the dry season. Decide first between siling haba, the long green finger chili for cooking, and siling labuyo, the small hot one. Hybrids bear more and for longer, while open pollinated labuyo keeps its heat and lets you save seed. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng gulay](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-gulay).

items.q: How long does it take to harvest?
items.a: It takes 60 to 80 days from transplanting to the first harvest. Then the weather and your care decide the exact day.
The record shows 7.79 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Hot Pepper?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
